text: Mark Mathabane's Kaffir Boy was banned in South Africa in 1986 under apartheid, for its depiction of life under the system and its use of language. Burlingame schools Superintendent Sonny da Marto later stopped a teacher from using it in her English classes, saying its paragraphs depicting child prostitution were inappropriate for 13- and 14-year-olds; he said he would allow an abridged version to be taught. In November 2008, some parents challenged the book for use in ninth grade English classes at Lincoln High School in Thief River Falls, MN, objecting to sexual violence and graphic language.
meta_description: Kaffir Boy by Mark Mathabane: banned in South Africa in 1986, stopped in Burlingame English classes, challenged in Thief River Falls, MN, in 2008.
